title: NSAT General Mock Test 04
description: Complete NSAT General mock test #4 with realistic exam experience. 80 questions across 6 sections.
instructions: Marking scheme: +4 for correct, -1 for incorrect
Answer all questions - no optional sections
Test is proctored via webcam and microphone

questions.questionText:
A delivery truck sets out from Warehouse A to deliver goods at Warehouse D. Along the route, it makes scheduled stops at two distribution hubs, Hub B and Hub C. The distances between A to B, B to C, and C to D are all the same.

Due to bad weather, the truck moves more slowly than usual:

From A to B, it travels at <inlineMath>\frac{3}{4}</inlineMath> of its regular speed.
From B to C, it travels at <inlineMath>\frac{4}{5}</inlineMath> of its regular speed.
From C to D, it travels at <inlineMath>\frac{5}{6}</inlineMath> of its regular speed.

By the time the truck reaches Hub B, it's already 40 minutes late. How many minutes late will the truck be by the time it reaches Warehouse D?

Consider a polynomial:
<blockMath>3{x^3} - 9{x^2} + kx - 12</blockMath>

If it is divisible by <inlineMath>\left( {x - 3} \right)</inlineMath>, then it is also divisible by which other factor?

Fresh cucumbers are composed of 96% water by weight. After being sun-dried, a portion of the water evaporates, reducing the water content to 95% of the total weight of the dried cucumbers. What percentage of the original weight is lost during this drying process?

Four departments in a company each employ 20, 40, 50 and 60 people. In these departments, the percentage of employees meeting their performance goals is 25%, 30%, 70% and 100%, respectively. What is the approximate overall percentage of employees in the company who achieved their performance goals?

In a company, 60% of the employees work in the technical department, while the remaining are in the administrative department. It is observed that 15% of the technical staff and 7.5% of the administrative staff receive a full performance bonus. If a total of 90 employees receive the full bonus, how many employees are eligible for a half-performance bonus, given that 50% of those who do not receive the full bonus qualify for the half bonus?
What is the value of <inlineMath>k</inlineMath> for which the sum of the squares of the roots of the quadratic equation <inlineMath>{x^2} + \left( {3 - k} \right)x + 2 = k</inlineMath> is minimized?
If you take the digits 2, 4, 5, and 6 and form all possible four-digit numbers where each digit is used only once, what would be the sum of these numbers?

In a charity event, 25 participants contributed money. The average contribution per participant was Rs 30. On average, the amount contributed by the women was Rs 5 more than that contributed by the men. When the organizer, who contributed an amount between Rs 64 and Rs 106, is included, the average contribution from all male members (including the organizer) becomes equal to that of the female members. If the average contribution of the men (in rupees) is a whole number, how many women participated in the event?

At a tech startup, 8 developers and 4 interns are to be assigned to three different project teams led by project managers Asha, Rohan, and Kabir. Two specific interns have expressed interest in working only with Rohan, while the remaining two interns have a conflict and cannot be placed on the same team.
If each team has equal members, in how many different ways can the 12 members be divided among the three project teams, while honoring these preferences and restrictions?

Meera runs an online clothing store. Her monthly revenue includes a fixed amount from a subscription-based model and a variable amount from regular sales. Two months ago, her variable sales revenue started growing rapidly due to increased marketing and online visibility.
In the first month, her variable revenue increased by 50%, followed by a 33.33% increase in the second month. As a result, her total monthly revenue is now 30% higher than what it was two months ago. What percentage of Meera’s revenue two months ago came from the fixed subscription model?

If Rina were to paint a wall by herself, she would need 27 more days than if she painted it together with her friend Meena. Conversely, Meena would need 3 more days to finish the wall alone than the number of days they would need working together. How many days can Rina and Meena complete the wall painting when they work on alternating days, starting with Rina?

In a shipment of 5 parcels, the average weight of the 4 lightest parcels is 50 kg, while the average weight of the 4 heaviest parcels is 55 kg. What is the difference between the maximum and minimum possible average weight of all 5 parcels?

In a particular region, each colony is identified by a natural number k . The population of a colony is (k+125), and each household in the colony consists of (k+5)  members. If no two colonies have the same number of households, what is the maximum number of such colonies that can exist in this region?

In a city, a cab charges a fixed amount along with a per kilometer rate. For a journey of 8 km, the total charge is Rs. 60, and for a journey of 12 km, the total charge is Rs. 85. After increasing the fixed charge by Rs. 5, what will be the charge for a 20 km journey under the new pricing structure?

What is the ratio of their total contributions to the charity funds, and how much money did each friend contribute if the total funds raised were Rs. 45,000?

A company sells a product at a profit margin of 25% on its cost price. However, due to changing market conditions, the company decides to apply a sequential discount strategy on the marked price as follows:
First, it increases the marked price by 20% over the original cost price.
Then, it offers a 15% festival discount on the marked price.
Finally, an additional loyalty discount of 10% is applied to the new price after the festival discount.
After applying both discounts, the final selling price becomes ₹2,754.

What was the original cost price of the product?
What is the overall percentage discount offered on the marked price?
If the company wants to maintain a 20% profit margin on the cost price, by how much should it increase or decrease the final selling price (₹2,754)?

At a week-long culinary workshop, seven different cuisine-themed sessions were organized from Monday to Sunday, one per day. The sessions were: Italian, Mexican, Chinese, Thai, Indian, French, and Japanese. 

Each session had a unique duration among 30 minutes, 45 minutes, 60 minutes, 75 minutes, 100 minutes, and 120 minutes, with exactly two sessions having the same duration.

The following information is known:
  1. The Chinese session lasted 45 minutes, but it was not held on Tuesday.
  2. The Thai and French sessions were held on consecutive days, with French before Thai, and the Thai session had the longest duration.
  3. Exactly two sessions were held between the Italian and French sessions.
  4. The duration of the Japanese and Italian sessions was the same.
  5. The Mexican session, which had the shortest duration, was held just before the Chinese session.
  6. The sessions held on Monday and Sunday were neither the longest nor the shortest in duration.
  7. The French session lasted 15 minutes more than the Japanese session, which took place on Sunday.
  8. The session on Monday lasted for 100 minutes.

What is the difference in duration between the Japanese and Indian sessions?

What is the sum of the duration of the session that immediately preceded the French session and the duration of the session that was held on Wednesday?

A third vehicle, Bike Z, starts from city B (midpoint) at the same time as Car Y, and moves towards A at 30 km/h.
At what distance from city A will Car X and Car Y meet?
At what time and distance from city A does Car X overtake Bike Z?

In a computer system, memory addresses are represented in hexadecimal. 

Hexadecimal System:
The hexadecimal (base-16) system uses digits 0-9 and A-F, where A = 10, B = 11, ..., and F = 15. It is often used in computing to represent large numbers (like memory addresses) in a more compact form than binary.
To convert hexadecimal to a decimal manually, you should first start multiplying the hexadecimal numbers by 16. Then, you raise it to a power of 0 and increase that power each time by 1 according to the hexadecimal equivalent system.

A program allocates a block of memory starting at address 7C5A1₁₆ and reserves 256 (₁₆) bytes of space. Find the new memory address after allocation in decimal?

Nine handbags of different colors, Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Grey, Black, White, Pink, and Brown, were displayed at a fashion exhibition. A water tank has a capacity of 12000 liters. It is being filled by three pipes: Pipe A, Pipe B, and Pipe C, and can be drained by Pipe D.
  • Pipe A fills the tank at a constant rate of 300 liters/hour.
  • Pipe B fills the tank at double the rate of Pipe A but is opened 2 hours after Pipe A.
  • Pipe C is a sensor-controlled pipe: it alternates between being on for 2 hours and off for 1 hour, repeating this cycle throughout. While on, it fills the tank at 400 liters/hour. It starts at the same time as Pipe A. But pipe C operates continuously until the tank fills after opening pipe D.
  • Pipe D is an outlet pipe and can empty 400 liters/hour, but it activates automatically when the tank is 77.5% full and runs continuously from that point onward until the tank is full.
All inlet pipes begin their schedule at 9:00 AM, except Pipe B, which starts at 11:00 AM.
At what exact time will the tank be completely full?

For how many of the given years is the Efficacy Ratio of at least two out of "Total Revenue" collections and "Property Revenue" collections greater than 1?

Arjun, Karan, Nilesh, Tanmay, Sohail, Rohan, Deepak, Viren, and Manish are seated in two parallel rows, with six seats in each row. Only nine people are seated, meaning there are three vacant seats in total. Each person seated in a row faces someone from the opposite row or a vacant seat. Vacant seats do not face each other.
Each of them prefers a different car brand, namely: Ford, Toyota, Hyundai, Tata, Skoda, Mahindra, Kia, Maruti, and Honda. The people seated in Row-1 face south, while those in Row-2 face north. The information is not necessarily in the same order.
  1. The person sitting third to the right of Rohan is facing the person or vacant seat that is immediate right of the one who prefers Maruti.
  2. Nilesh is an immediate neighbor of vacant seats.
  3. Exactly one person sits between the ones who like Kia and Maruti.
  4. Rohan and the one who prefers Hyundai are facing each other.
  5. Sohail sits second to the right of the person who likes Tata.
  6. The people who like Toyota and Mahindra are immediate neighbors.
  7. Manish, who likes Skoda, is not adjacent to any vacant seat.
  8. The person who prefers Toyota and the one who prefers Honda are seated facing each other.
  9. Karan and Arjun, who likes Hyundai, sit diagonally opposite to each other.
  10. The number of persons to the right of Sohail equals the number of persons to the left of Tanmay.
  11. Rohan's favorite car brand is Tata.
  12. The one who likes Ford sits third to the right of the one who likes Toyota.
  13. Viren likes neither Maruti nor Kia.
  14. Deepak sits immediately to the right of Nilesh, who does not face south.
Who among the following sits opposite to the person sitting second to the left of Sohail?

Area for each surface of a regular tetrahedron can be obtained using the formula <inlineMath>\frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{4}{d^2}</inlineMath>.

A school is forming teams for an inter-school quiz competition. There are 8 students, 4 boys and 4 girls. A team of 4 students is to be selected and seated in seats numbered 1 to 4. The conditions are:
  • Each team must have at least 2 boys and at least 1 girl.
  • The oldest boy must be seated in seat 1 or seat 2.
  • The youngest girl cannot be seated next to the oldest boy.
In how many ways can such a team be selected and seated?

Ravi, a garment retailer, increases the price of all jackets in his store by 25% above their cost price. He offers a 20% discount on 3/5th of the jackets, and a 15% discount on 1/5th of the jackets. If Ravi earns an overall profit of 5%, then the percentage of discount that he must offer on the remaining jackets is ____%?

Launched in 2015 by the Government of India, the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao (BBBP) campaign aims to address the declining child sex ratio and promote the education and empowerment of girls. Rooted in growing concerns over gender discrimination and female foeticide, the initiative seeks to create awareness at the grassroots level and improve girls’ access to education. Through joint efforts by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and the Ministry of Education, the program integrates advocacy, enforcement of legal measures, and local community involvement.

While the campaign has received praise for spotlighting gender inequality, critics argue that implementation gaps and insufficient funding limit its long-term impact. Nonetheless, BBBP remains a symbolic and strategic effort toward a more inclusive and gender-equal society.

Which of the following best supports the objectives of the 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' initiative?

options.text: Encouraging early marriage to protect girls from urban risks.
Promoting gender-sensitive education and community awareness programs.
Limiting girls’ access to co-educational institutions.
Offering incentives only to families with male children.

questions.questionText:
A national economic policy refers to the strategic framework a government uses to control the country’s financial activities and growth. It typically includes rules on taxation, government spending, financial law, trade, and markets. The predominant dreams are to obtain stable financial growth, control inflation, lessen unemployment, and equitable earnings distribution. Governments might also undertake either expansionary or contractionary policies depending on the monetary cycle. For instance, during a recession, expansionary guidelines like accelerated public spending and tax cuts may be used to stimulate demand. 
 

Conversely, to combat inflation, contractionary policies may include raising interest rates or reducing government spending. A sound financial policy strikes a balance between short-term measures and long-term planning to maintain fiscal discipline and support sustainable development. 

What is the best summary of the passage above?

options.text: National economic policy focuses only on reducing government spending and raising interest rates.
National economic policy is a strategy for managing a country’s economy through various tools to promote stability and growth.
National economic policy deals exclusively with controlling inflation through monetary measures.
National economic policy aims to increase taxes and restrict public spending to ensure fiscal control.

questions.questionText:
The end of the monarchy in France was not merely the result of a single event but the culmination of deepening crises layered across decades. The rigid structure of the Ancient Régime had long placed privilege in the hands of a narrow aristocracy, while the majority languished under oppressive taxation and limited rights. Intellectual ferment sparked by Enlightenment thinkers like Rousseau and Voltaire questioned the very legitimacy of divine-right rule, igniting philosophical unrest among the emerging bourgeoisie and disillusioned lower classes.

However, the monarchy might have withstood ideological dissent had it not been for the mounting economic turmoil. War debts, food scarcity, and skyrocketing bread prices bred desperation. King Louis XVI’s indecisiveness and failure to enact meaningful reforms alienated both moderates and radicals. The convening of the Estates-General in 1789, meant to offer solutions, instead exposed the deep fissures within French society. Popular anger spilt into the streets, culminating in the storming of the Bastille—a symbolic rejection of tyranny.

As revolutionary fervour spread, the monarchy’s authority eroded rapidly. The eventual execution of Louis XVI in 1793 was less an isolated act of defiance than the logical consequence of years of injustice, disconnection, and failed adaptation. The end of the monarchy in France was thus not accidental; it was the inevitable effect of a system unable or unwilling to evolve.

Which statement most accurately reflects a complex cause-and-effect relationship underlying the collapse of the French monarchy, as inferred from the passage?

options.text: The monarchy’s reliance on divine right and suppression of reform ignited a chain of intellectual dissent that directly culminated in the king’s execution.
The convergence of economic hardship, political inertia, and philosophical awakening catalysed a revolutionary shift that dismantled monarchical rule.
Revolutionary leaders exploited Enlightenment rhetoric to manufacture unrest, thereby orchestrating the monarchy’s fall for political gain.
Foreign wars and external debts overshadowed domestic discontent, forcing the monarchy to dissolve under international pressure.

questions.questionText:
Romanticism, a cultural and intellectual movement that emerged in the late 18th century, marked a dramatic departure from the rational ideals of the Enlightenment. Romantic thinkers, artists and writers championed emotion, imagination and individualism, seeking to express a deeper connection with nature, the sublime and human experience. Figures such as William Wordsworth, Samuel Taylor Coleridge and Lord Byron emphasised the importance of personal intuition and the beauty of the natural world, while composers like Beethoven and Chopin pushed the boundaries of music to evoke emotional depth. The movement also arose as a reaction against the Industrial Revolution, which many Romantics viewed as dehumanising. Yet, despite its emphasis on freedom and emotional expression, Romanticism was not without its contradictions. Some Romantic thinkers romanticised the past, often overlooking the darker aspects of history, while othersidealised rebellion and revolution, yet struggled with the practical outcomes of these ideals. While Romanticism inspired profound cultural and artistic contributions, its idealism sometimes clashed with the harsh realities of the political and social changes of the time.
Which of the following higher-order inferences best aligns with the passage’s portrayal of Romanticism?

options.text: Romanticism was an intellectual rebellion against Enlightenment rationalism, celebrating emotion and nature while at times ignoring the complex political and social realities
Romanticism was a predominantly idealistic movement that successfully addressed the social and political issues of the time through its focus on emotion and individualism.
Romanticism’s celebration of the past and nature led to a political movement that achieved tangible, lasting changes in the social structures of Europe.
Romanticism was primarily an artistic movement with little impact on the broader intellectual, philosophical, political and economic trends of the 19th century.

questions.questionText:
In a democracy, it is essential that government policies related to elections promote fairness, participation, and trust in the system. These policies usually cover areas like campaign financing, voting procedures, and how voting districts are drawn. While such measures aim to make elections free and fair, they can sometimes unintentionally benefit certain political groups. 

For instance, rules that limit campaign donations are meant to prevent corruption, but they may also make it harder for smaller parties to compete with larger ones that already have recognition and resources. Similarly, changing voting districts to reflect population shifts can improve representation, but it can also be used to favour particular political parties—a tactic known as gerrymandering. 

Even rules requiring voter ID, designed to reduce fraud, may discourage some eligible voters from participating. Thus, while these policies are often presented as neutral, their real-world effects must be examined closely to ensure they do not harm the democratic process they are meant to protect.

Based on the passage, which of the following statements best captures the underlying concern the author raises about election-related policies in democratic systems?

options.text: Although election policies such as campaign finance limits, redistricting, and voter ID laws are intended to promote fairness and prevent misuse, their practical outcomes can unintentionally benefit certain political groups. Therefore, these policies must be regularly evaluated to ensure they do not weaken the democratic values they aim to protect.

Election regulations that involve financial restrictions, voter identification, and district changes are fundamentally flawed in design. To preserve true democracy, such policies should be eliminated entirely, as they consistently disadvantage vulnerable political voices.

Since democratic governments are formed by majority rule, any election-related policies they create naturally reflect the people’s will. Even if some groups feel disadvantaged, these outcomes are a necessary part of how representative democracy functions.

The real issue with elections is not the structure of policies but the unequal media coverage and funding that political parties receive. Unless every party is given equal exposure and resources, election fairness cannot be achieved, regardless of policy adjustments.

questions.questionText:
Swami Vivekananda, an Indian spiritual leader and philosopher, emphasised the importance of self-realisation, universal brotherhood, and service to humanity. His teachings advocated for a balanced life that integrated spiritual growth with social responsibility. He believed that education should build character, strengthen the mind, and develop the capacity to face life’s challenges with confidence. Vivekananda's message resonated across boundaries, inspiring millions to embrace the idea of unity in diversity and inner strength. 

He consistently urged the youth to believe in themselves and to work not just for personal gain but for the upliftment of society at large. His words, such as “Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached,” remain a powerful call to action even today.

Which of the following best supports the central ideas expressed in the passage?

options.text: True education is about scoring high marks to achieve financial security and fame.
Social change begins when individuals prioritise self-interest over community service.
Youth must channel their potential toward societal good, rooted in self-belief and moral strength.
Spiritual pursuits must be separated from practical life in order to maintain focus.

questions.questionText:
Liberty, a core concept in political philosophy, refers to the condition in which individuals have the freedom to act according to their own will, within the boundaries of law and social order. Classical liberal philosophers like John Locke emphasised negative liberty, the absence of external restraints, especially from the state. In contrast, later thinkers like T.H. Green introduced the idea of positive liberty, where true freedom involves the ability to realise one's potential through access to education, health, and fair opportunity.

The concept of liberty has evolved with changing political contexts, from the struggle against monarchies to the demands for democratic rights and social justice. In modern democracies, liberty is protected through constitutions, legal rights, and institutions that prevent the concentration of power. However, political philosophers continue to question how liberty should be balanced with equality, security, and the public good, making it a dynamic and contested idea in political thought.

Which of the following options presents a supporting and an opposing argument regarding the concept of liberty as discussed in the passage?

options.text:
Supporting: Liberty ensures complete individual autonomy with no restrictions.
Opposing: Liberty should be absolute, even if it harms others.

Supporting: Liberty allows individuals to act freely within legal and social boundaries.
Opposing: Too much liberty may need to be limited to maintain equality and the public good.

Supporting: Liberty only applies to political leaders, not to ordinary citizens.
Opposing: Liberty must be removed to strengthen national unity.

Supporting: Liberty is effective only when backed by military power.
Opposing: Liberty weakens the state and should be replaced by strict control.

questions.questionText:
Cognitive literature, as an example, examines how human beings’ process information, make selections, and form memories. Behavioural psychology, stimulated via researchers like B.F. Skinner, makes a speciality of observable moves and how they're formed by using external reinforcements.

Psychoanalytic literature, rooted in the works of Sigmund Freud, researches into the unconscious, emphasising the function of adolescence and hidden goals in shaping personality. On the other hand, humanistic psychology, championed by figures like Carl Rogers, prioritises self-actualisation, inherent growth, and emotional well-being over deterministic views of conduct.

More modern-day psychological literature integrates neuroscientific findings, cultural views, and social dynamics, reflecting the evolving nature of mental inquiry. While these procedures fluctuate, they share a not unusual aim: to understand and interpret the human psyche, supplying deeper insights into private and societal improvement.

Based on this, which of the following most accurately reflects why psychology as a discipline must continuously adapt and refine its literature?

options.text: The complexity of human cognition and behaviour cannot be fully understood through a single theoretical lens, requiring an ongoing synthesis of emerging perspectives, empirical research, and interdisciplinary insights.
While older psychological theories retain their foundational value, new discoveries primarily serve to reinforce pre-existing frameworks rather than introduce novel paradigms or methodologies.

The rapid advancement of neuroscience and technology has rendered many classical psychological theories obsolete, necessitating a complete departure from historical frameworks in favour of biologically driven explanations.
Psychological literature remains largely static, but external factors such as cultural shifts and technological advancements occasionally require reinterpretation of its core principles.

questions.questionText:
The Partition of Bengal in 1905, planned by the British under Lord Curzon, was a pivotal moment in the history of Indian nationalism. This event, officially justified as an administrative measure, was widely perceived as a deliberate attempt to divide Bengal along religious lines, weakening the unity of the growing nationalist movement. The move sparked widespread protests across India, with leaders and citizens alike condemning it as an act of colonial manipulation. The Swadeshi Movement emerged in response, urging Indians to boycott British goods and promote indigenous industries. This period marked a significant shift in the tone of Indian nationalism, moving from moderate petitions to more assertive resistance. Despite the eventual reversal of the partition in 1911, the event left an indelible mark on the nationalist psyche, fuelling a stronger and more united demand for self-rule.

After reading the passage, select the correct tone of the passage.

Antarctica, one of the most remote and extreme environments on Earth, presents significant challenges for scientific research. However, recent innovations in technology are transforming how polar research is conducted, allowing scientists to explore the frozen continent with greater speed, accuracy, and safety. One key advancement is the use of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), which can navigate beneath thick ice sheets to collect data on ocean temperature, salinity, and marine life. These robotic tools allow researchers to access previously unreachable areas without endangering human lives. 

Drones and solar-powered weather stations are also playing vital roles by collecting atmospheric data and monitoring remote areas continuously, even in harsh weather. Advances in communication technology now allow scientists in Antarctica to share findings quickly with teams around the world, speeding up collaboration and decision-making.

Which of the following statements best supports the passage’s main idea about the role of technology in Antarctic research?

options.text: Cutting-edge tools like drones and AUVs help researchers explore remote polar regions more efficiently and safely, advancing scientific understanding.
The harsh environment of Antarctica makes the use of modern technology unpredictable and risky.
Reliance on automated systems limits human judgement, making scientific findings less reliable.
Traditional exploration techniques offer a more authentic experience than technology-driven research.

questions.questionText:
Entrance exams, though often viewed with anxiety, can positively influence a student's intellectual and emotional development. These exams encourage disciplined study habits, time management, and goal-setting skills that are valuable throughout life. They challenge students to think critically, solve problems efficiently, and apply concepts in practical ways. Preparing for such exams also nurtures resilience and determination, as students learn to cope with pressure and setbacks. 
While competition can be intense, entrance exams provide a merit-based opportunity for students to showcase their abilities and earn access to higher education and better career prospects, ultimately fostering self-confidence and a growth mindset. 
Which of the following statements best reflects a positive effect of entrance exams, as described in the passage?

options.text: Entrance exams, though stressful, help students build problem-solving and goal-setting abilities.
Entrance exams create pressure that can negatively affect students’ academic confidence.
Entrance exams promote intense competition, often overshadowing true talent.
Entrance exams rely heavily on content memorisation rather than analytical reasoning.

questions.questionText:
Venice, the enchanting city of canals, masks, and timeless beauty, is as mysterious as it is historic. Beneath its romantic surface lies a deep tapestry of legends, secrets, and unanswered questions that have captivated travellers and historians for centuries. The city’s maze of narrow alleyways and fog-covered waterways creates an atmosphere ripe for intrigue, where truth and myth often intertwine. From the legend of the haunted island of Poveglia, once a quarantine zone and plague hospital, to whispered tales of secret societies meeting in candle-lit palazzos, Venice is a city that guards its secrets well.

The Carnival masks, now symbols of festivity, once served to conceal identity and social class, allowing citizens to indulge in behaviours otherwise forbidden. Stories of ghostly gondolas, lost treasure beneath the lagoon, and cryptic codes in ancient Venetian buildings continue to stir imaginations. Even the city’s slow sinking into the sea adds to its mystique; an eternal place fading into time. Whether it’s the silent passage of a gondola at midnight or the faded frescoes of a forgotten church, Venice remains a city where the line between reality and legend is delightfully blurred. Its mysteries are not just tales of the past; they are part of its living, breathing soul.

Which of the following best summarises the central idea of the passage?

options.text: While Venice is admired for its visual beauty and cultural heritage, its deeper appeal stems from the enigmatic blend of legend, secrecy, and the haunting passage of time.
Venice’s unique architecture and carnival traditions alone have allowed it to retain historical significance despite its gradual submersion.
The passage reveals that Venice's image as a mysterious city is largely manufactured for modern tourism and lacks historical grounding.
Venice has transitioned from a place of myth to one of rational urban decline, where facts now replace the need for stories and speculation.

questions.questionText:
In a world dominated by rapid technological progress, expanding economies, and algorithmic logic, the concept of humanity has become paradoxically both more visible and more endangered. The term "humanity" today extends beyond acts of compassion—it encompasses the moral reasoning that challenges convenience, the empathy that resists apathy, and the self-awareness that questions even our noblest intentions.

Modern expressions of humanity are increasingly tested not in moments of physical survival but in moral ambiguity. Consider a developer designing AI that could automate millions of jobs—does one prioritise efficiency or human livelihoods? Or a policymaker allocating vaccines during a shortage should citizens be prioritised over stateless refugees? These dilemmas reveal that humanity is not merely the presence of kindness but the courage to confront complexity with integrity, even when solutions are imperfect.

Throughout history, civilisations have defined humanity in contrast to cruelty and indifference. Yet in contemporary times, cruelty often wears the mask of neutrality, hidden in systems that operate without accountability or in decisions justified as economically sound but socially devastating. True humanity, then, may lie not in the act but in the intention, not in outcomes but in the willingness to bear moral responsibility.

Importantly, humanity is not just about others; it is also a mirror. How societies treat the marginalised, the voiceless, or even the inconvenient, reflects how deeply humanity has been internalised, not as charity, but as a principle that disrupts indifference. Thus, to be truly humane today is to act consciously in systems that reward detachment, to ask the difficult questions, and to remain accountable for answers we may never fully resolve.

Which of the following statements most accurately captures the philosophical tension presented in the passage?

options.text: Although acts of compassion are valued, the real test of humanity lies in reconciling individual ethical commitments with the often impersonal demands of large systems that prioritise efficiency over moral consequence.

In modern society, maintaining neutrality in decision-making is the most effective way to avoid bias, as it ensures equitable treatment across groups, regardless of moral complexity or emotional appeal.
The evolution of technology and data-driven systems has created an environment where personal accountability is unnecessary, since outcomes are driven by algorithms rather than human choices.
True expressions of humanity now rest solely on international policymaking and large-scale humanitarian frameworks, rather than on the ethical behaviour of individuals within daily systems of power.

questions.questionText:
The Earth’s ever-changing surface is largely the result of tectonic plate movement, a slow but powerful force that has shaped continents, formed mountains, triggered earthquakes, and created ocean basins over millions of years. The planet’s lithosphere is divided into rigid plates that float atop the semi-fluid asthenosphere. Driven by forces such as mantle convection and gravitational pull, these plates continuously shift, collide, diverge, and slide past each other.
At convergent boundaries, Earth's plates push against each other. This can form huge mountains like the Himalayas or deep valleys in the ocean. At divergent boundaries, the plates move away from each other. This lets hot, melted rock come up and make new land, like along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. At transform boundaries, the plates slide past each other sideways. This can cause strong earthquakes, like the ones near California’s San Andreas Fault.
Which of the following best summarises the central idea of the passage?

options.text: Tectonic plates are solely responsible for creating natural disasters like earthquakes and volcanoes.
The Earth's surface remains stable unless acted upon by volcanic eruptions at divergent plate boundaries.
The ongoing movement of tectonic plates is a fundamental force that continuously transforms Earth’s surface and holds vital clues to both its past and future.
Tectonic activity has mostly ceased in modern times, leaving behind static landforms and stable crustal boundaries.

questions.questionText:
The invention of X-rays transformed healthcare allowing doctors to diagnose fractures, detect lung infections, and even locate foreign objects within the body without surgical procedure. This appreciably reduced the need for invasive tactics, making clinical remedy safer and more efficient. Beyond medicinal drugs, X-rays are also used in protection screening, astronomy, and fabric evaluation, proving their effect across more than one field.

However, early X-ray use came with risks. Scientists and medical doctors were ignorant of the harmful results of extended exposure to radiation, leading to accidents and fitness issues. Over time, improvements in protective strategies and safety guidelines helped decrease these dangers, ensuring that X-rays stay an essential device in present-day technology and medication.

Which of the following best describes a cause-and-effect relationship from the passage?

options.text: The accidental discovery of X-rays led to major advancements in medical diagnosis and reduced the need for invasive surgeries.
The invention of X-rays made other scientific discoveries unnecessary, limiting further advancements in medical imaging.
The discovery of X-rays was planned by Roentgen to create a tool for diagnosing fractures.
The harmful effects of early X-ray exposure caused scientists to abandon its use in medical fields.

questions.questionText:
Beauty is often thought of as subjective—"in the eye of the beholder"—but scientific studies show that our notion of beauty isn't always entirely random. From the symmetry of facial functions to the golden ratio in layout, research in psychology and biology has proven that our brains respond to positive patterns as extra aesthetically desirable. These responses aren't merely emotional; they're grounded in evolutionary instincts tied to health, fertility, and environmental harmony.

Modern science no longer defines beauty it has all started to form it. With improvements in cosmetics, dermatology, and even AI-generated aesthetics, the standards of beauty have accelerated dramatically. Scientific formulation now powers skincare products, while algorithms can predict how adjustments in looks can also affect social perception.

However, this scientific influence on beauty is not without its tensions. As technology begins to define what is considered beautiful, there is a risk that natural diversity may be overshadowed by artificial standards. The more we can measure and modify appearance, the more we must ask ourselves: Is beauty becoming more inclusive and democratic, or is it increasingly controlled and standardised?

Ultimately, science is not eliminating the mystery of beauty; it is reshaping its boundaries. Sometimes this leads to empowerment and self-expression, but at other times it raises deep ethical questions about authenticity, identity, and societal pressure.

 

Based on the passage, which of the following is the most accurate inference about the relationship between science and beauty?

options.text: While scientific advancements have expanded our understanding and manipulation of beauty, they also introduce the risk of promoting narrow and artificial standards that may unintentionally suppress natural diversity and cultural variation.

The increasing scientific control over beauty suggests that emotional and cultural interpretations of attractiveness are becoming outdated and will likely be replaced by universally accepted, measurable standards.

The progress of science in shaping beauty is a sign that society is moving toward a more inclusive and equitable definition of attractiveness, one that allows everyone to conform more easily to established ideals.

Scientific involvement in beauty has eliminated subjective judgments by creating tools and metrics that offer complete clarity, thereby ending longstanding debates around what is considered beautiful.

questions.questionText:
William Wordsworth, one of the central figures of English Romanticism, revolutionised poetry by turning away from the lavish language and rigid forms of the 18th century. Instead, he embraced simplicity, emotion, and nature as the heart of poetic expression. Born in 1770, Wordsworth’s deep connection with the natural world became the cornerstone of his poetic vision. He believed that nature was not only a source of beauty but also a moral and spiritual guide, capable of healing the human soul and awakening profound truths.
Wordsworth's collaboration with Samuel Taylor Coleridge on Lyrical Ballads in 1798 marked a defining moment in literary history. In this collection, he argued that poetry should reflect the language of ordinary people and the experiences of everyday life. His most famous works, such as Tintern Abbey and Ode on Intimations of Immortality, explore themes of memory, childhood, loss, and the sublime power of nature. His verses, infused with sincerity and reverence, continue to inspire generations with their quiet strength and philosophical depth.
Which of the following statements best supports the viewpoint expressed in the passage about William Wordsworth’s contribution to poetry?

options.text: Wordsworth’s emphasis on natural imagery and emotional depth made poetry more accessible and meaningful to the common reader.
Wordsworth’s rejection of traditional poetic forms weakened the structural beauty and discipline of classical poetry.
True poetry should maintain its complexity and elevated diction to distinguish it from everyday speech.
By simplifying language and focusing on nature, Wordsworth diminished poetry’s potential to explore deeper intellectual themes.

questions.questionText:
Summer holidays are regularly considered as a pause from instructional rigour; however, under the surface, they function as a crucial phase in a scholar's holistic improvement. These extended breaks from training environments offer more than just relief from tests and early mornings, they create space for emotional recalibration, social exploration, and highbrow curiosity past textbooks. In the absence of inflexible schedules, students often rediscover autonomy, make impartial choices, and have interactions in unstructured play, all of which are essential for developing executive functioning and emotional intelligence.

Moreover, summer time holidays offer possibilities for experiential learning, be it through a tour, creative pursuits, volunteering, or even boredom. These stories can deepen empathy, spark innovation, and inspire risk-taking in safe environments. Psychologists argue that such non-linear learning paths are essential for intellectual fitness, as they nurture a sense of self-confidence, reduce overall performance stress, and repair the natural rhythm of formative years often disrupted via consistent competition.

Which of the following inferences can be reasonably drawn from the passage, based on the underlying assumptions and implications presented?

options.text: The long duration of summer breaks is primarily justified by academic fatigue, and thus, shortening them could enhance continuous learning without affecting student well-being.
Structured academic environments are superior for psychological growth since they offer predictable routines and reduce the uncertainty that comes with unstructured time.
Summer holidays, when effectively utilised, can play a transformative role in shaping emotional maturity, creativity, and mental health, although these benefits are not guaranteed for all students.
Students from resource-rich backgrounds are more likely to benefit from summer breaks, making the idea of universal holidays less equitable and in need of restructuring towards skill-based camps.

options.text: The complexity of human cognition and behaviour cannot be fully understood through a single theoretical lens, requiring an ongoing synthesis of emerging perspectives, empirical research, and interdisciplinary insights.
While older psychological theories retain their foundational value, new discoveries primarily serve to reinforce pre-existing frameworks rather than introduce novel paradigms or methodologies.

The rapid advancement of neuroscience and technology has rendered many classical psychological theories obsolete, necessitating a complete departure from historical frameworks in favour of biologically driven explanations.
Psychological literature remains largely static, but external factors such as cultural shifts and technological advancements occasionally require reinterpretation of its core principles.
